clue.text: Filing put off, thus raising the spirits

indicators.note: off in the sense of gone wrong or not right signals that these letters are jumbled

parts.note: fodder taken as written
fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Putting off the filing is a cheering thought for an office worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks as if it belongs with 'put' (put off, postponed), but it is the anagram signal on FILING PUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cheering lifts the mood, which is exactly what raising the spirits means.

clue.text: Discourage and head off armed criminal

indicators.note: taking the head off a word removes its first letter here

parts.note: a gunman is a criminal carrying a weapon

explanation.surface: Police dissuade and intercept a robber carrying a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head off' reads as intercept, but it says to lose the first letter of GUNMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To deprive someone of courage or nerve is to dishearten them.

clue.text: Coming down from the top of the stairs

definitions.meaning: an aircraft's descent to the ground ends in this
the flat area at the head of a staircase

explanation.surface: Someone descends from the upstairs hallway.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrival on the ground after flight, and also the level floor space where a staircase ends.

clue.text: Stuff — as happens in police canteens

definitions.meaning: to cram food into someone against their will
a whimsical reading: the police force getting its feed, a meal for the force

explanation.surface: Stuffing oneself, as officers do at their station canteen.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeding someone by compulsion is to cram them; the second sense splits the term into the constabulary plus a meal.

clue.text: Racial claim by me — an unlikely alternative!

definitions.text: Racial claim by me — an unlikely alternative!

parts.words: Racial claim by me — an unlikely alternative!
parts.note: a speaker declaring their nationality as being from the Netherlands, which is also the stock phrase said after an incredible condition: if that is so, then I am from Holland

explanation.surface: Someone states their ethnicity, offered as an improbable option.
explanation.walkthrough: The British idiom 'if that's true, I'm a Dutchman' expresses total disbelief; read literally, it is a claim about one's own nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is literally a statement of one's nationality and idiomatically a scoffing rejection of something unlikely.

clue.text: Concert could go either way

indicators.note: a word reading the same forwards and backwards can be read in either direction

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A performance whose outcome is uncertain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could go either way' sounds like an uncertain result, but it says the word is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: A gig is a live musical performance by a band.

clue.text: Being cheated was painful

definitions.meaning: having been swindled or overcharged, informal
smarted, as from an insect's sting

explanation.surface: Being swindled hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquially a person overcharged has been fleeced; literally the word describes something that smarted.

clue.text: Intelligence of Elinor Dashwood's novel contribution

definitions.meaning: in Jane Austen's novel the sensible elder sister Elinor embodies the first quality of the title, Marianne the second

explanation.surface: A character's wisdom is what she adds to the book.
explanation.walkthrough: Elinor Dashwood is the sister in Austen's Sense and Sensibility who stands for the first word of the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Good judgement is the quality of shrewdness; Elinor supplies it in the Austen title.

clue.text: Swell at university gets second, with prompting

parts.note: being up means in residence at university, especially Oxford or Cambridge
an urge is an inner prompting

explanation.surface: A student at university gets a second-class degree after encouragement.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a student is 'up' at university; 'second' suggests a degree class but gives only S.
explanation.definitionFit: A swell is a rise or increase, as is a sudden surge upward.

clue.text: Big hit is a tricky achievement

definitions.meaning: a baseball home run with the bases loaded
winning every trick in bridge, or all the major tournaments in tennis or golf

explanation.surface: A huge success is hard to pull off.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball, a bases-loaded home run; in bridge, taking all thirteen tricks.

clue.text: One who's pitted against a goddess?

parts.note: a miner works in a pit, a coal mine
V is short for versus, against

explanation.surface: Someone is set in opposition to a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitted' suggests matched against an opponent, but it means working in a pit, as a coal miner does.
explanation.definitionFit: Minerva was the Roman deity of wisdom.

clue.text: Agent is new broom

indicators.note: making a new version of the letters means rearranging them

parts.note: fodder taken as written
fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: A spy is a new kind of cleaning implement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broom' looks like a sweeping brush, but it is the shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Genista is the botanical genus of yellow-flowered shrubs known as broom.

clue.text: Sound hooter when one interrupts

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into something, so this letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: hooter is British slang for the nose
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A car horn blares when someone cuts in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hooter' suggests a car horn, matching 'Sound', but it is slang for a nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Noise is any audible din or racket.

clue.text: Brief statement about Lenin's nephew still kept secret?

definitions.text: Brief statement about Lenin's nephew still kept secret?

parts.words: Brief statement about Lenin's nephew still kept secret?
parts.note: a nephew of Lenin might tersely remark that his mother's brother is a Communist; read differently, the run of words means not yet released or approved

explanation.surface: A short remark about a revolutionary's relative remains confidential.
explanation.walkthrough: To Lenin's nephew, Lenin is his uncle, and a Bolshevik is a Red: a terse 'Uncle: a Red' run together gives the answer; the question mark flags the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not given official clearance is still restricted, not yet approved for release.

clue.text: Managing to rock part of wall

parts.note: coping means managing, getting by
a stone is a piece of rock

explanation.surface: Somehow getting by enough to shake a section of masonry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' looks like a verb, shake, but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The top course of a wall is made of these protective slabs.

clue.text: Drink tea, say

definitions.meaning: a ... is a measure of spirits, as in a ... of whisky
said aloud this sounds like tee, the small support a golfer sets a ball on

explanation.surface: Have a drink, a cup of tea for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition works by sound: 'tea' said aloud is tee, the golf ball's support.
explanation.definitionFit: A small measure of spirits, and also a little pin like a golf tee.

clue.text: Original sin, say, from early times

indicators.note: say signals a word spoken aloud rather than written

parts.note: original means primal, and a sin is an evil

explanation.surface: Original sin dates from the dawn of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Original sin' is the Christian doctrine, but here it gives primal evil, which spoken quickly sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Primaeval means belonging to the earliest ages of the world.

clue.text: Avoid turn as part of watch

parts.note: to escape something is to avoid it
to wheel is to turn round

explanation.surface: Dodge the turn while keeping guard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'watch' could be a sentry's duty, but it is the timepiece.
explanation.definitionFit: The toothed wheel in a timepiece's escapement regulates the release of the mainspring's energy.

clue.text: What's wife to fit over hip, say?

definitions.text: What's wife to fit over hip, say?

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits over the next

parts.note: hale means fit and healthy
the hip is one example of a bone

explanation.surface: Asking what a wife wears to fit snugly over the hips.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: the stiffening of old corsets fitted over a woman's hips.
explanation.definitionFit: Baleen from whales was used to stiffen corsets shaped to the waist and hips.

clue.text: Let article join all the baggage

parts.note: a let is a hindrance or obstruction, as in 'without let or hindrance'
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Permit some item to be added to the luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let' looks like permit, but here it is the old noun meaning obstacle.
explanation.definitionFit: Impedimenta are cumbersome equipment and luggage carried along on a journey.

clue.text: The best was first to be drunk

parts.note: the pick of something is the best of it
led means was in front, came first

explanation.surface: The top competitor was the first one to become intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickled is slang for intoxicated, as if preserved in alcohol.

clue.text: Section of the military — three-quarters of it

indicators.note: keeping three of four letters drops the last quarter of the word

parts.note: it refers back to the military, the army

explanation.surface: Part of the armed forces makes up most of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' points back to the military, which is the army; three-quarters of its four letters is the first three.
explanation.definitionFit: An arm of the services is a branch such as the air force or infantry.

clue.text: Stagger to us and collapse

indicators.note: collapsing letters fall apart and are rearranged

parts.note: fodder taken as written
fodder taken as written
fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone lurches towards us and falls down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stagger' reads as reel, but here it means amaze.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger someone is to amaze or shock them.

clue.text: Disasters in some aspects of grammar reported

indicators.note: reported speech is something said, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: accidence is the part of grammar dealing with inflections of words

explanation.surface: Catastrophes found in the reporting of grammatical points.
explanation.walkthrough: Accidence, the study of word inflections, sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mishaps and calamities are unforeseen misfortunes.

clue.text: Tempted to put name on bottom of picture

indicators.note: in a down clue placing a letter at the bottom puts it after the other part

parts.note: to draw is to picture

explanation.surface: An artist feels the urge to sign their name at the foot of the painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Being drawn to something means being attracted or lured by it.

clue.text: One who's tucked into pie — ate ravenously?

definitions.text: One who's tucked into pie — ate ravenously?

indicators.note: the letters sit tucked into the words that follow, spanning them

explanation.surface: Someone who wolfed a pie gobbled it greedily.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'piE ATE Ravenously'; the whole clue also describes the answer, a diner who has tucked into pie.
explanation.definitionFit: A diner who has devoured food is a consumer of it.

clue.text: One's going too fast to be trapped by this

definitions.text: One's going too fast to be trapped by this

parts.words: One's going too fast to be trapped by this
parts.note: speeding motorists are caught by a police speed trap using a detection device

explanation.surface: A speeding driver gets caught by the police device.
explanation.walkthrough: Police speed traps use this detection system; the answer also reads the same either way.
explanation.definitionFit: The radio-wave system used in speed traps detects how fast cars are moving.

clue.text: Brave sort of Latvian

indicators.note: a sort of something is a variant of it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: A courageous kind of Baltic citizen.
explanation.definitionFit: Courageous and heroic people are described as bold.

clue.text: Make use of bathroom fixture

definitions.meaning: to exploit or draw on a resource
a valve fitting over a basin or bath

explanation.surface: Use the plumbing in the bathroom.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit a resource, and also the faucet over a sink.

clue.text: Pompous old stick carries weight when speaking

indicators.note: a word that carries another holds it inside

parts.note: a rod is a stick

indicators.note: spoken aloud, the unit of mass is heard as a homonym, a cask

parts.note: a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A self-important elderly man with a cane is influential when he talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carries weight' reads as being influential; 'carries' is the container signal and 'when speaking' turns ton into its sound-alike, the wine cask.
explanation.definitionFit: Orotund speech is bombastic and self-important in style.

clue.text: The French teacher was enticing

parts.note: le is French for the
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: The French tutor was seductive.
explanation.definitionFit: To lure someone along is to tempt them, so a past participle phrase matches.

clue.text: Claimant's quiet about proposal

definitions.note: read as claimant is, so the definition is just the claimant

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
re means about, concerning
a tender is a formal offer or bid

explanation.surface: A person suing keeps silent regarding an offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone asserting a right to a throne or title is a claimant to it.
